title: race during kernel handoff causes KV-slab overlap and length-dependent token bias
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: After landing an aggressive kernel routing optimization that does non-blocking handoff between fused-attn and fallback-attn kernels, we observed reproducible, length-dependent token skew in long streaming completions. The output divergence is small per-token but accumulates over >1024 tokens leading to visible semantic drift and higher perplexity for affected models. This ticket tracks the investigation and remediation.
impact: Affects hosted and dedicated inference when mixed-precision quantized kernels are eligible for runtime fallback. Customers with long-context streaming (>=1k tokens) may see degraded generation quality and higher error rates for hallucination-sensitive prompts. Regression surfaced in synthetic long-context regression tests and in one customer report (private) with an LLM summarization pipeline.
reproduction_steps: 1) Checkout runtime branch containing recent scheduler change (commit 9f3a4c2).
3) Observe deterministic token divergence from baseline at token ~870 and persistent divergence thereafter.
4) Capture GPU traces with nvprof/NSight and runtime traces via dd-trace: traces show interleaved kernel-launch timestamps around the handoff boundary.
5) Run with RT_ASSERT_KV_ZERO=1 to observe immediate crash or corruption in KV slab when concurrency window is hit.
hypothesis: The kernel scheduler issues a fallback kernel launch without a full fence/serialization of KV slab metadata updates. Under high concurrency (concurrent prefill + decode) the slab allocator writes (tail pointer updates) can interleave with fallback kernel writes, producing overlapping KV indices. Because fused-attn and fallback-attn use slightly different numeric accumulation (order of ops and mixed-precision paths), the overlapped region produces small fp discrepancies which amplify through softmax normalization across long sequences.
experiments: A) Reproducer amplified by toggling concurrency: reducing decode concurrency to 1 removes the divergence => points to race with concurrent prefill workloads.
B) Inserted explicit cudaDeviceSynchronize() before kernel handoff: divergence disappears, but latency increases by 6-12% in microbenchmarks.
C) Zeroing a small suffix of the KV slab on handoff (cheap memsets) prevents overlap and removes divergence in test runs — low perf impact but is a band-aid.
D) Built variant with atomic compare-and-swap on slab tail updates: fixes correctness but performance regression under high throughput workloads.
E) Ran long regression across 50+ model/seq combos in CI: failure correlates with models that use grouped attention tiling and quantized matmul fallback paths.
temporary_mitigation: Reverted the non-blocking handoff on the rollout channel (feature-flag disabled). Deployed a conservative fallback that inserts a lightweight fence on kernel selection if concurrent prefill workers are active. Added emergency Canary to detect recurrence (datadog monitor: infra.runtime.kv.handoff.errors).
next_steps: 1) Design: update kernel scheduler to maintain per-request handoff epoch counters and perform ordered commits to KV slab metadata (Arjun + Nicole) — target: deterministic handoff without global fences.
2) Engineering: implement epoch-based slab-commit protocol with relaxed memory ordering (PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12984).
3) Tests: add fuzz harness that exercises interleaved prefill/decode schedules and long-context streams; add a regression job in main CI that runs the reproducer nightly.
4) Perf: microbench and tune to recover lost throughput from epoch protocol; explore per-shard light-weight atomics instead of full CAS on the hot path.
5) Postmortem: write incident blameless postmortem and update runtime stability dashboard with token-drift metrics.
6) Release plan: patch to runtime-1.22, staged canary for Dedicated customers, full rollout after 2 days of canary stability.
